statement: There exists a one-layer log-precision nonlinear MLP RNN that exactly recognizes unary-encoded sorted deterministic graph connectivity, which is L-complete under FO reductions. Conditional on not every language in L admitting polynomial-size bounded-fan-in Boolean circuits of depth o(log^2 n), some such log-precision nonlinear RNN requires Omega(log^2 n) circuit depth to simulate.

existential: one fixed one-layer nonlinear MLP RNN
universal: every valid unary-encoded sorted deterministic graph-connectivity instance
quantifiers.obligation: The RNN accepts exactly the reachable instances using O(log n)-bit state values.

conditional_assumption: Not every language in L has a polynomial-size bounded-fan-in Boolean circuit family of depth o(log^2 n).
assumptions: Each source vertex has at most one outgoing edge.
Edges are ordered by strictly increasing source label and point forward in the topological order.
Vertices, source, and target are unary encoded with separators.
Counter values are integers and the ReLU MLP is evaluated exactly at O(log n) precision.
Deterministic graph connectivity is L-complete under FO reductions.

primary_reference.title: Problems complete for deterministic logarithmic space
primary_reference.authors: Stephen A. Cook and Pierre McKenzie

pass_condition: The layered FO-reduction schema preserves reachability, determinism, and sortedness; the counter invariant is reconstructed; the explicit ReLU zero mask is exact on integers; counter magnitudes imply O(log n) bits; the independent exhaustive checker covers its complete finite domain; the one-layer-copy control fails; and the depth conclusion remains explicitly conditional.
fail_condition: Any source mismatch, derivation mismatch, reduction counterexample, zero-mask error, precision-bound error, negative-control pass, or dropped conditional assumption exits nonzero.
limitations: The certificate proves the construction and conditional implication; it does not resolve the open circuit lower bound for L. The exhaustive checker is a bug detector over a complete bounded domain, while the universal result comes from the parametric invariant and layered-reduction proof schema.
